title: Labels I'm not certain about in Bitwig 6

blocks.html: Researched October 2026. Bitwig hasn't published a version 6 user guide yet, so each answer below was checked against the Bitwig 5.3 user guide, the official 6.0 and 6.1 release notes, and third-party sources only where those two are silent. Type correction, partly or still open in the filter box to see one group.

Summary: 43 items: 30 resolved (26 confirmed, 4 that correct the guide), 8 partly answered, 5 still open. For anything unresolved, holding Bitwig's Interactive Help over the control shows its official name.

Guide correction Sampler's One-shot is not a playback mode. The Play Mode menu holds Repitch, Cycles, Textures, Spectral and Fragments. One-shot is an option of Envelope Mode, alongside Gated. Before 6.1 the same setting was called Shot. Source: Bitwig 6.1 release notes; Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.24.5

Guide correction Removing a modulation routing is a right-click, not a double-click. Right-click the modulator's routing button and click the ✕ beside the target (or Delete to clear all). Or right-click the target knob and click ✕ under MODULATION ROUTINGS. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 16.2.1

Guide correction Loud Split splits by loudness, not frequency. Its bands are Quiet (green), Mid (yellow) and Loud (red), set by a Higher Threshold and a Lower Threshold, each with its own Knee. It's in the Spectral category. Any step that treats it as a crossover needs rethinking. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.23.3

Guide correction To-Da-Choppa doesn't appear to exist. It isn't in the 5.3 manual, the 6.0 or 6.1 release notes, or anywhere online. Bitwig's built-in Vocoder (Filter category: Modulator and Carrier chains, 8 to 80 bands) does what Part 12 describes. Check what the device is called on your screen. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide, Bitwig 6.0 release notes, Bitwig 6.1 release notes, web search

Confirmed Where the project-wide key signature is set (Part 1). New in 6.0: Root Note and Scale in the Transport, 23 scales, with automation lanes at the top of the Arranger. In the piano roll, K turns on Snap to Key. Source: Bitwig 6.0 release notes
Confirmed Where the velocity lane lives. The Note Expression Lane under the notes (press V). It also shows Chance and Release Velocity. Source: Bitwig 6.0 release notes

Partly answered Clip loop length and the 7-sixteenth display. The clip header in the Detail Editor has a loop bar: double-click turns looping on or off, drag to adjust. The Inspector has a Loop section too. Not yet known: the exact readout format for a 7-sixteenth length. Source: Bitwig 6.0 release notes; Bitwig 5.3 user guide 5.4

Confirmed How cue markers are added. Right-click the Beat Ruler and turn on Show Cue Markers, then right-click again and choose Insert Cue Marker. Insert Cue Marker Here can be given a shortcut in Dashboard > Shortcuts. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 5.5.1

Confirmed Whether Ctrl+G / Cmd+G groups selected tracks. Yes. Ctrl+Shift+G (Cmd+Shift+G) ungroups. In 6.0 the same keys also turn a time selection of automation into an automation clip. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide ch. 3; Bitwig 6.0 release notes
Confirmed Whether clips can opt out of global groove. Yes. Each clip has a Shuffle toggle and an Accent % in the Inspector's Shuffle section. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 5.4.6
Confirmed Whether the per-note pitch lane reads Pitch or Transpose. Both: it's labelled Pitch / Transpose (press P). Source: Bitwig 6.0 release notes
Confirmed Drum Machine choke groups (Part 16.7). Yes. Right-click a chain and use the Choke targets or Choked by submenu. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 16.1
Confirmed Whether global shuffle swings 16ths or 8ths (Part 16.7). Either. The global groove Rate is 1/8 or 1/16, and Shuffle delays the even-numbered steps. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 14.3
Still open What "pre" means on a sidechain source. Bitwig's docs don't define it. Third-party write-ups suggest either before the volume fader or before the track's effects. Source: not documented

Partly answered The Steps modulator's controls. Has step count, direction (forward, backward, ping-pong), polarity and phase. Trigger modes: Transport, with Groove, Free running, Note / Restart, Note / Random. Not yet known: how bars are drawn, and whether 7 can be typed in directly. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.28.7.3
Still open Reverb's parameter names, especially mix. The manual only names the EARLY and TANK sections and the Tank FX and Wet FX chains. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.20.2

Confirmed Delay+'s feedback control and "EQ" knobs. The control is Feedback (0 to 122%). The feedback tone controls are low-pass and high-pass filters; the manual doesn't call them EQ. Patterns are Mono, Stereo, Ping L and Ping R. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.6.1

Partly answered The Arpeggiator's mode names. 17 patterns, plus Octave Behavior modes Broad, Thin and 1 by 1. Not yet known: the pattern names, and whether one matches Ableton's "play order". Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.17.1
Confirmed Phaser+'s Manual Override toggle. Manual Override. It switches off the internal LFOs and exposes a Mod knob for your own modulation. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.16.5
Confirmed Polymer's wavetable position knob. Index. A toggle next to it switches interpolation off. Source: MusicTech and Bonedo tutorials (third-party)

Confirmed Where Polymer's Glide and mono settings live. Glide is on the device's front panel. Mono is in the Inspector: set Voices to 1, then choose True Mono or Digi Mono, with Retrigger and Steal same key options. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.24.3, 16.2.4.1

Partly answered Wrapping a device in an Instrument Layer from the right-click menu. Forum users report that Ctrl+G (Cmd+G) on selected devices wraps them in an FX Layer or Instrument Layer. Not in Bitwig's docs. Source: KVR forum (community)
Confirmed A native pitch-shift device for 12.13's FB FX slot. Yes: Pitch Shifter (frequency, Grain, Mix). Freq Shifter and Freq Shifter+ also exist. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.2.4

Confirmed Whether Delay+ holds forever and stops runaway loops. Forever (snowflake icon) holds the feedback buffer at unity with no new input. Level Control (Soft Clip, Hard Clip or Comp., with a Threshold) keeps the loop from exploding. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.6.1

Confirmed Whether Delay+'s Time can be unsynced. Yes. Time can be set in seconds as well as beats. Time Update Model Repitch glides audibly; Fade hides the pitch artifacts. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.6.1

Confirmed Sampler's 6.1 phase-modulation character. In Cycles mode, choose the Phase modulation character. Controls: Mod (depth) and Harm (modulator tuning). Repitch also gained Clean, Analog and Digital characters. Source: Bitwig 6.1 release notes

Partly answered Resonator Bank's per-band controls and key tracking. Six filters, each with frequency, resonance and gain, plus global morph controls and key tracking that follows incoming notes. Not yet known: whether pitch is in semitones or Hz. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.11.5
Confirmed Whether there's a standalone Comb device. Yes: Comb (frequency plus bipolar feedback). Comb modules also exist in Filter+, Polymer and The Grid. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.11.1
Still open Whether Delay+ goes short enough for Karplus-Strong. The shortest delay time isn't documented. Delay-1 and an FX Grid delay remain the fallbacks. Source: not documented

Guide correction Where Loud Split lives and how its bands are labelled. Spectral category. See the correction above: it splits by loudness (Quiet, Mid, Loud), not frequency. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.23.3

Confirmed Whether an ADSR on an effect after Sampler fires on the track's notes. Yes. Instruments and audio effects pass the notes they receive on to later devices and modulators, so Setup B works as written. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 13.3 note on hybrid tracks

Confirmed Whether a Chain container accepts Sampler. No. Chain is audio in, audio out. Instrument Layer (notes in, audio out) is the right container, as the guide's fallback already says. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.4.1, 19.4.4
Confirmed Amp's model names. Bitwig's own names, such as Class AB, Eulic and Fold B. None match Ableton's Bass, Blues or Boost. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.7.1
Confirmed Whether Delay-2 has independent left and right times. Yes: separate time, offset and feedback per side, plus Detune, Rate and Crossfeed. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.6.3

Confirmed The Grid's module names for wavefolding, AM and phase/FM. Wavefolder (Shaper), AM/RM (Level) or Multiply (Math). Phase-1 and Pitch Shift have phase/FM inputs; the 6.1 Sampler module adds a Repitch Phase In port. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.29; Bitwig 6.1 release notes
Still open The TR-8S instrument names in 16.4. These come from blurry screenshots; only the original reels can settle them. Source: n/a

Partly answered Closed and open hat on the same step (Pattern 3, step 15). User reports agree the closed hat wins and chokes the open hat. On the TR-8S choke is set per instrument, so it can vary by kit. Source: MusicRadar, Roland Clan forum
Confirmed Note operator names in version 6. Chance, Repeats (plural), Occurrence and Recurrence, in the Inspector's Operators section when notes are selected. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide ch. 12

Confirmed Reaching Remote Controls and MIDI mapping. Remote Controls is a button in each device header (an icon of six controls). To map, right-click a knob and choose Learn Controller Assignment…. The Mappings Browser panel lists and edits all mappings. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 15.1.1, 15.3, 15.4

Partly answered Recording a Launcher performance and automation into the Arranger. The record-to-Arranger options are in the Play menu, Clip Launcher section. In 6.0, recording Launcher clips also writes automation by default. Not yet known: the exact click-by-click steps. Source: Bitwig 6.0 release notes

Confirmed Whether Bounce in Place is in the clip's right-click menu. Yes. Since 5.x it comes in Pre-FX, Pre-Fader and Post-Fader versions, and in 6.0 it works on group tracks' meta clips too. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 13.2; Bitwig 6.0 release notes

Partly answered The Peak Limiter's parameter names and true-peak detection. Input Gain, Ceiling and Release. Nothing anywhere mentions true-peak detection, so Part 11's assumption that it has none still stands. Source: Polarity's Peak Limiter guide (third-party); Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.9.6

Still open The label of Over's Delta toggle. Delta mode exists (Threshold becomes the level above which you hear signal), but the toggle's on-screen label isn't documented. Source: Bitwig 5.3 user guide 19.7.4
Confirmed Tilt or EQ+ shelves for master-bus tone. Still a matter of taste, as the guide says. Source: n/a

Compressor+'s Character chooser does exist, but displays its current value (Vanilla by default) rather than a "Character" label. Treemonster's controls (Threshold, detector low-pass and high-pass, Pitch, Speed, Ring, Mix) match Bitwig's user guide and the on-screen device. Delay+ has a Ping mode and an EQ section, visible on the device during the Rubby Wubby build.
Everything else in this guide was verified during the build, and Part 11's device descriptions came from Bitwig's published user guide.

Bitwig Studio User Guide 5.3 (bitwig.com/userguide, PDF, February 2025). Bitwig 6.0 and 6.1 release notes (downloads.bitwig.com/6.0/Release-Notes-6.0.html, downloads.bitwig.com/6.1/Release-Notes-6.1.html). Third-party: Polarity's Peak Limiter guide (polarity.me), MusicTech and Bonedo Polymer tutorials, KVR Bitwig forum, MusicRadar's TR-8S guide, Roland Clan forum.
